thread:
tarek: FYI I pulled an nsys capture on the staging runner — we have ~250-350us extra per-request after the new NVTX ranges landed. Trace looks like we’re pushing/popping ranges for every KV cache lookup.

sasha: ouch. are those per-kv access ranges explicit calls in runtime now? @tarek can you paste the snippet you used to instrument?

tarek: yep, we added a helper in kvcache::trace_span that does nvtxRangePushA/Pops around the prefetch + lookup. snippet: ```cpp
nvtxRangePushA("kvcache:lookup:shard-" + std::to_string(shard_id));
... lookup code ...
nvtxRangePop();
```

liam: that string concat is allocating in the hot path — definitely a perf smell. Also NVTX string metadata ends up in the timeline and can inflate CPU work.

sasha: can we use static range names + an int id payload instead? NVTX supports ranges with integer payloads via nvtxEventAttributes_t. Something like: ```cpp
nvtxEventAttributes_t attr = {};
attr.version = NVTX_VERSION;
attr.size = NVTX_EVENT_ATTRIB_STRUCT_SIZE;
attr.colorType = NVTX_COLOR_UNKNOWN;
attr.category = KVCACHE_CATEGORY; // small enum
attr.payloadType = NVTX_PAYLOAD_TYPE_UNSIGNED_INT;
attr.payload.unsignedInt = shard_id;
nvtxRangePushEx(&attr);
```

perf-bot: nsys summary: mean per-request delta = +312us (95th +420us), top CPU hotspots: std::string ctor, nvtxRangePushEx, snprintf in logging.

liam: agree on using static labels + payload. Also we should avoid pushing ranges for every internal kv lookup; that's too high cardinality. We only need request-level boundary, and one small prefetch span aggregated per-request.

tarek: the original intent was to make kernel selection visible per lookup to map kernel choices to cache hits. But the overhead is not worth it. Options: (1) request-level range only, (2) aggregated counters + occasional sample ranges, (3) use a sampling profiler mode that enables fine-grained NVTX only when a debug flag is set.

sasha: my vote: default to request-level boundary (low-cost), add a dynamic sampling gate env var RUNTIME_NVTX_FINE=1 that turns on per-kv ranges for a fraction of requests (e.g., 1%). We can implement sampling via RNG on request id so it's deterministic.

liam: +1. Also change naming convention: "runtime/request/<req_id>" for top-level, and "runtime/kvcache:op:<kind>" as static labels for sampled finer ranges. Avoid runtime string allocation: use a small fixed char buf with snprintf for request id only at request-level, and for kvcache use category+payload.

perf-bot: quick nsys command that helped reproduce: ```bash
nsys profile -o nvtx_kv_test --trace=cuda,nvtx --sample=none --capture-range=nvtx --stop-on-exit --stats=true ./bench_runner --workload=kv_heavy
```

infra-bot: noted. creating a short-lived feature flag on staging: feature/kv-nvtx-sampling. Will roll it to 1% and run nightly load test.

tarek: action items: 1) revert per-kv string ranges -> implement static ranges + payload (tarek). 2) add RUNTIME_NVTX_FINE sampling with deterministic hash (sasha). 3) run nsys perf regression job and post perfetto link (liam). I'll open a PR with the nvtx helper change and benchmark before/after.

sasha: tiny naming proposal for the PR: use categories and labels below — keep short to reduce timeline noise: ["rt:req", "rt:kvc:prefetch", "rt:kvc:lookup"], and put request id as payload only on rt:req.

liam: ack. If we want kernel-level visibility, we can later tag GPU kernel launches with nvtxRangePushEx with kernel enum — cheaper than string concat.

tarek: thanks. I'll target the PR for EOD today. If perf-bot still shows >100us regression after changes, we'll revert and instrument via sampled traces only. :thumbsup:
